As the John Ternus era unfolds, Apple is undergoing more high-level personnel changes. A new report from Bloomberg today indicates that Apple has appointed a new head of mergers and acquisitions (M&A), as well as a new vice president of the App Store.

9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: A wide range of Sony BRAVIA TVs are offering major discounts, covering entry-level to flagship models — buy now and save instantly!

The report states that Apple has appointed Steve Smith as the new head of mergers and acquisitions. Smith will succeed Adrian Perica, who joined Apple in 2009 and led the M&A and corporate development team for over a decade. Bloomberg describes Smith as Perica's "longtime deputy." He will report to CFO Kevan Parekh.

Meanwhile, Perica will take on a "more significant role" within Apple's Services division. He has been responsible for iCloud, Fitness+, and Apple News since 2023, and will report directly to services chief Eddy Cue going forward.

In fact, both Perica and Apple Music head Oliver Schusser are seen as potential successors to Cue:

Additionally, Bloomberg also reported today that Apple will promote Carson Oliver to vice president of the App Store, reporting to Cue. Until stepping down in August this year, the App Store had been overseen by Apple Fellow Phil Schiller.
